title: Arms Sales Notification
items_summary: Enhancement/upgrade of a previously notified (Transmittal 24-63) sale of 12 UH-60M Black Hawk helicopters, 30 T700-GE-701D engines, and related equipment, adding ARC-231A SATCOM radios, AGM-114R2 Hellfire and AGM-179A JAGM missiles, APKWS-II guidance sections, CIRCM, DVEPS, EGI, AN/APR-39E(V)2, and other items.

summary: This Section 36(b)(5)(C) report notifies Congress of an enhancement to the Government of Sweden's 2024 Black Hawk helicopter case (Transmittal 24-63), which adds Hellfire and JAGM missiles, APKWS-II guidance sections, CIRCM infrared countermeasures, DVEPS, ARC-231A SATCOM radios, EGI navigation units, and other items. The estimated MDE value rises by $700 million to $1.2 billion, and the total case value rises by $1.3 billion to $2.2 billion. The stated justification is to strengthen a NATO Ally that contributes to political stability and economic progress in Europe, and the enhancement adds communications and cryptographic capability. The notice also records an earlier May 22, 2025 enhancement (Transmittal 0E-25) that added ARC-231A SATCOM radios and EGI units without changing the $900 million total case value.

DEPARTMENT OF DEFENSE

Office of the Secretary

[Transmittal No. 26-1K]


Arms Sales Notification

AGENCY: Defense Security Cooperation Agency (DSCA), Department of 
Defense (DoD).

ACTION: Arms sales notice.

-----------------------------------------------------------------------

SUMMARY: The DoD (referred to herein as ``the Department,'' 
``Department of War'' or ``DoW'') is publishing the unclassified text 
of an arms sales notification.

FOR FURTHER INFORMATION CONTACT: Urooj Zahra at (703) 695-6233, 
[email protected], or [email protected].

SUPPLEMENTARY INFORMATION: This 36(b) arms sales notification is 
published to fulfill the requirements of section 155 of Public Law 104-
164 dated July 21, 1996. The following is a copy of the attached 
Transmittal 26-1K.

    Dated: November 17, 2026.
Stephanie J. Bost,
Alternate OSD Federal Register Liaison Officer, Department of Defense.
Transmittal No. RSAT 26-1K

REPORT OF ENHANCEMENT OR UPGRADE OF SENSITIVITY OF TECHNOLOGY OR 
CAPABILITY (SEC. 36(B)(5)(C), AECA)

    (i) Purchaser: Government of Sweden
    (ii) Sec. 36(b)(1), AECA Transmittal No.: 24-63
    Date: May 29, 2024
    Implementing Agency: Army
    (iii) Description: On May 29, 2024, Congress was notified by 
congressional certification transmittal number 24-63, of the possible 
sale, under Section 36(b)(1) of the Arms Export Control Act, of twelve 
(12) UH-60M Black Hawk helicopters; thirty (30) T700-GE-701D engines 
(24 installed, 6 spares); and seventeen (17) AN/AAR-57 counter missile 
warning systems. The following was also included: AN/APR-39C(V)1/4 
radar warning receivers; AN/AVR-2B laser detecting sets; AN/ARN-149(V) 
low frequency automatic direction finder radio receivers; AN/ARN-153 
tactical air navigation system receiver transmitters; AN/APN-209 radar 
altimeter; EBC-406HM emergency locator transmitters; enhanced ballistic 
armor protection systems; internal auxiliary fuel tank systems; fast 
rope insertion extraction system; external rescue hoist; rescue hoist 
equipment sets; Martin Baker palletized crew chief and gunner seats 
with crashworthy floor structural modifications; aircraft fire 
extinguisher cartridge; impulse cartridge; thruster TCU-3/A; helmets; 
transportation; organizational equipment; spare and repair parts; 
support equipment; tools and test equipment; technical data and 
publications; personnel training and training equipment; U.S. 
Government and contractor engineering, technical, and logistics support 
services; and other related elements of logistics support and program 
support. The estimated total cost was $900 million. Major Defense 
Equipment (MDE) constituted $500 million of this total.
    On May 22, 2025, Congress was notified by congressional 
certification transmittal number 0E-25, of the possible sale of sixteen 
(16) ARC-231A RT-1987 very high frequency (VHF)/ultra-high frequency 
(UHF)/line-of-sight (LOS) satellite communications (SATCOM) radios; 
twenty-nine (29) embedded global positioning system/inertial navigation 
system +429. The following non-MDE items were also included: ARC-231 
RT-1808A VHF/UHF/LOS SATCOM radios; APX-123A identification friend or 
foe (IFF)

[[Page 75316]]

transponder (or future IFF replacement); AN/PYQ-10 simple key loader; 
KIV-77 common IFF crypto applique; AN/ARC-201D RT-1478D radios; and 
other related elements of logistics and program support. The addition 
of MDE did not result in a change to estimated MDE value which remained 
$500 million. The total case value did not increase and remained $900 
million.
    This transmittal notifies the inclusion of the following MDE items: 
up to one hundred (100) AGM-114R2 Hellfire Missiles; up to one hundred 
(100) AGM-179A Joint Air-to-Ground Missiles; up to one hundred fifty 
(150) WGU-59/B Advanced Precision Kill Weapon System-II guidance 
sections; up to thirty (30) common infrared countermeasures; up to 
twenty (20) degraded visual environment pilotage systems (DVEPS); up to 
seventy (70) ARC-231A RT-1987 VHF/UHF/LOS SATCOM radios; up to thirty 
(30) embedded global positioning systems/inertial navigation system 
(EGI EAGLE M+429) or future replacement; up to thirty (30) AN/APR-
39E(V)2 radar warning receivers; and up to fifty (50) M240H machine 
guns. The following non-MDE items will also be included: GAU-19 Gatling 
guns; M134D-H mini-guns; A965 cartridge, 25.4MM decoy M839; LA14 decoy, 
infrared countermeasure M211 with decal; H843 warhead, 2.75in M151 
high-explosive rocket; HA07 rocket motor, 2.75in MK66; HA10 rocket, 
2.75in infrared flare with warhead M278 and fuze; M442 and motor MK66; 
HA13 rocket, 2.75in practice with warhead M274 and safe and arming 
device M423 and rocket motor MK66; HB03 rocket, 2.75in fl[eacute]chette 
with warhead M255A2 and rocket motor MK66; L410 flare, aircraft 
countermeasure IR M206; M514 fuze, proximity; MD66 cartridge, impulse 
CCU-44/B; MG62 cartridge, impulse BBU-35/B; Hydra 70 rocket launchers; 
M260 rocket launchers; M261 rocket launchers; M299 rocket launchers; 
infrared laser; captive carry training missiles; Alkan Bomb Racks; 
configurable lightweight wing; MX-15D electro optical infrared sensors; 
AN/PRC-160; AN/PRC-167; small tactical terminal (STT) KOR 24-A; video-
oriented radio transceiver for the exchange of information (VORTEX) 
transceiver; APX-123 identification friend or foe; helmet display 
tracking system; computer weapon management system; and other related 
elements of program and logistic support.
    The estimated MDE value will increase by $700 million to a revised 
$1.2 billion. The estimated non-MDE value will increase by $600 million 
to a revised $1 billion. The estimated total case value will increase 
by $1.3 billion to a revised $2.2 billion. MDE constitutes $1.2 billion 
of this total.
    (iv) Significance: The inclusion of this MDE represents an increase 
in capability over what was previously notified. The proposed articles 
and services will provide Sweden an additional advanced communication 
and cryptographic capability to address current and future 
requirements, reinforcing Sweden's ability to maintain regional 
stability and improve its security.
    (v) Justification: This proposed sale will support the foreign 
policy and national security objectives of the United States by 
improving the security of a NATO Ally that is a force for political 
stability and economic progress in Europe.
    (vi) Sensitivity of Technology:
    The AGM-114R2 missile is used against heavy and light armored 
targets, thin-skinned vehicles, urban structures, bunkers, caves and 
personnel. The missile is inertial measurement unit-based, with a 
variable delay fuze, improved safety and reliability. The highest 
classification level for release of the AGM-114R2 is Secret. Software 
and firmware documentation, such as data processing, software 
requirements, source code, algorithms, height of burst sensor, are not 
authorized for disclosure. The highest level of classified information 
that could be disclosed by a proposed sale or by testing of the end 
item is up to and including Secret. The highest level that must be 
disclosed for production, maintenance, or training is up to and 
including Secret. Vulnerability data, countermeasures, vulnerability 
and susceptibility analyses, and threat definitions are classified as 
Secret or Confidential. Detailed information to include discussions, 
reports and studies of system capabilities, vulnerabilities and 
limitations that lead to conclusions on specific tactics or other 
countermeasures are not authorized for disclosure. Reverse engineering 
could reveal Secret information. Loss or compromise of classified 
information associated with the AGM-114R2 could lead to development of 
countermeasures or exploitation of system vulnerabilities by those 
obtaining the information.
    The Joint Air-to-Ground Missile all up round, designated AGM-179A, 
is an air-to-ground missile (AGM) consisting of a Hellfire-Romeo (AGM-
114R) back-end (i.e., propulsion, warhead, and control sections) mated 
to a newly designed dual-mode guidance section (GS). The dual-mode GS 
is a combination of millimeter wave (MMW) and semi-active laser (SAL) 
sensors co-axially aligned on a steerable gimbal. The combination of 
MMW and SAL sensors provide improved precision point and fire-and-
forget capabilities onto a single munition. This combination allows 
targeting capability against fast moving and stationary targets in 
countermeasure and/or a battlefield intensive environment, and in low 
cloud ceiling and adverse weather. Firing modes include lock-on before 
launch and lock-on after launch. Engagement modes include point 
designation--SAL only; target designation--SAL initiated with MMW 
engagement completion; active fire-and-forget laser queuing--MMW 
initiated with SAL override capability; active fire and forget--MMW 
only. Hosting platforms include rotary-wing, select fixed-wing, 
wheeled/tracked vehicles, ground-based pedestal launcher, and patrol 
boats. Lethality includes tactical armor, boats, bunkers, buildings, 
caves, personnel in open, rotary and slow fixed wing; unmanned aircraft 
systems, non-tactical vehicles-fast moving. The MMW is capable of 
hitting low radar cross section targets.
    The Advanced Precision Kill Weapon System (APKWS-II) is a design 
conversion of an unguided Hydra 2.75-inch rocket with a laser guidance 
kit to give it precision-kill capability. As a low-cost weapon, it is 
intended as an inexpensive means to destroy targets while limiting 
collateral damage in close combat. The APKWS consists of an APKWS-II 
guidance section developed by BAE systems, legacy 2.75-inch MK66 Mod 4 
rocket motor, and a legacy MK151 and MK435/436 warhead/fuze. These 
guided rockets are steered to the target by following reflected laser 
beam energy directed onto the target either by the launching aircraft, 
a second aircraft, or ground-based troops operating a laser designator. 
The APKWS is a tactical rocket system that can be launched from several 
platforms, including rotary wing, fixed wing, and ground-based 
vehicles, offering multi-mission, multi-target capability, and 
precision-strike lethality.
    The Common Infrared Countermeasure (CIRCM) is the next-generation 
lightweight, laser-based, infrared countermeasure system for rotary-
wing, tilt-rotor, and small fixed-wing aircraft across the DoD. CIRCM 
provides near spherical coverage of the host platform to defeat 
infrared (IR)-seeking threat missiles. CIRCM receives an angular 
bearing hand-off from the common missile warning system, employs a 
pointing and tracking system that acquires and tracks the incoming 
missile. CIRCM jams the missile by using modulated laser energy, thus

[[Page 75317]]

degrading the tracking capability of the missile and causing it to miss 
the aircraft.
    DVEPS provides overmatch by providing increased situational 
awareness to the aircrew in Degraded Visual Environment (DVE) 
conditions such as brownout, allowing special operations aviation 
assets to execute missions in almost any environmental condition. 
Utilizes using three-dimensional (3D) imaging technology. DVEPS 
produces imagery, 3D conformal symbology, and system alerts to aid 
pilots in maintaining spatial awareness during and after transition 
from visual meteorological conditions (VMC) to degraded visual 
environment (DVE) conditions. DVEPS includes synthetic vision avionics 
backbone, light detection and ranging, removable storage device, 
infrared camera, power distribution unit, and inertial measurement 
unit.
    The AN/ARC-231A is a software-definable radio for military aircraft 
that provides two-way, multi-mode voice and data communications over a 
30 Hz to 512 MHz frequency range. No designated exportable/non-
communication security capable version planned. Support both line-of-
sight UHF and VHF bands with amplitude modulation, frequency 
modulation, and SATCOM capabilities including embedded frequency agile 
modes, electronic counter-countermeasures anti-jam waveforms including 
HAVEWQUICK and SINCGARS, demand assigned multiple access, integrated 
waveform. It provides simultaneous, real-time participation in tactical 
voice and data communications networks. The RT-1987 will provide NSA 
TSVCIS 3.1.1crypto modernization compliance. Operator selectable air 
traffic control channel spacing of 5, 8.33, 12.5, and 25 kilohertz 
(kHz) steps, and other data link and secure communications features; 
providing battlefield interoperability.
    The EGI EAGLE M+429 provides GPS and INS capabilities to the 
aircraft. The EGI will include selective availability anti-spoofing 
module (SAASM) security modules to be used for secure GPS precise 
positioning service, if required. The EAGLE M+429 contains sensitive 
technology that provides GPS hardening when loaded with COMSEC keys.
    The AN/APR-39E(V)2 radar warning receiver is a radar threat 
detection system that passively detects, categorizes, and prioritizes 
radio frequency threats to aircraft, and then provides an audio/visual 
cue to aircrew. AN/APR-39E(V)2 provides a fully digital capability to 
enhance threat discrimination in the MMW) band and increased overall 
system performance against frequency-agile RF and active electronically 
scanned array threat radars.
    The APX-123 transponder is Mark XIIA common transponder containing 
an NSA-certified M4/M5 crypto and meets all U.S. and NATO mode 4 and 5 
requirements. When installed in conjunction with platform antennas the 
transponder provides identification, altitude, and surveillance 
reporting in response to interrogations from airborne, ground-based 
and/or surface interrogators. The transponder provides operational 
capabilities for Mark XIIA IFF capabilities of Modes 1, 2, 3/A, C, 5 
level 1 and level 2, and Mode S (levels 1, 2, and 3 capable). 
Additionally, the transponder incorporates Automatic Dependent 
Surveillance Broadcasts (ADS-B) Out capability.
    The 1305-A965, CTG, 25.4mm, Decoy M839 & 5865-Z133 is a chaff, 
countermeasure M1. The M1 (Z133) is a 25.4mm decoy chaff cartridge. The 
Z133 is a component in A965. All cartridge components including the 
cartridge case, piston, end cap and theoretical band coverage are 
UNCLASSIFIED. The specifications and the drawings for this item are 
also UNCLASSIFIED. Radar cross section measurements of deployed chaff 
are CONFIDENTIAL. Chaff deployment timing, sequence, pattern and 
effectiveness against radar threats are SECRET/NOFORN.
    The 1370-LA14, M211 & 1370-LA15, M212 flares are unclassified, the 
associated technology is sensitive and can be reverse engineered. The 
performance/effectiveness can defeat certain U.S. shoulder-launched 
missiles. No technical data packages or test information should be 
supplied.
    The small tactical terminal (STT) KOR-24A is used to provide 
airborne, maritime, fixed station small airborne link 16 terminal 
capability. The STT is the latest generation of small, two-channel, 
Link 16 and VHF/UHF radio terminals. While in flight, the STT provides 
simultaneous communication, voice or data, on two key waveforms. The 
Link 16 data link is a military tactical data link network. Link 16 
provides aircrews with enhanced situational awareness and the ability 
to exchange target information to command and control (C2) assets via 
tactical digital information link-joint. The Link 16 can provide a 
range of combat information in near-real time to U.S. and allies' 
combat aircraft and C2 centers. This system uses high assurance 
encryption.
    The AN/PRC-160 radio is a tactical wideband high frequency (HF)/VHF 
transceiver providing Type 1 encryption and SAASMGPS location and 
timing capabilities. The system provides continuous frequency coverage 
from 1.5 to 60 megahertz. The manpack version provides 20 watts HF and 
10 watts VHF transmit power from a single battery. The system transmits 
in bandwidths from 3 kHz to 24 kHz with data rates up to 120 kilobits 
per second. The software programmable system can operate using NATO 
standard 2G, 3G, and 4G automatic link establishment waveforms and is 
compatible with AM single sideband and CW modes. As a Type 1 secure 
system, the AN/PRC-160 is considered an unclassified controlled 
cryptographic item (CCI).
    The AN/PRC-167 is a multi-domain multi-channel tactical narrow and 
wide-band dual transceiver radio system providing Type 1 encryption and 
SAASM GPS location and timing capabilities. The system can provide 
wide-band high-assurance self-healing networking capabilities and 
mobile user objective system over-the-horizon capabilities. Each 
transceiver is software programmable operating in the 30-512 MHz and 
764-2600 MH frequency ranges. The system can operate using the 
following waveforms: narrow-band analog/PCM AM/FM, CVSD ASK/FSK cipher 
text, wideband 2400 bps and LPC/2400 MELP-SATCOM. As a Type 1 secure 
system, the AN/PRC-167 is considered an unclassified CCI.
    The VORTEX Sc variant is a secure, real time full motion video 
(FMV) and data transmission system that provides enhanced situational 
awareness, surveillance, and battle damage assessment for U.S. and 
coalition air and ground forces. VORTEX Sc enables aircrews, unmanned 
aircraft operators, and ground elements to exchange live video and 
mission data with U.S. and coalition platforms, including large 
airframes, unmanned aerial vehicles targeting pods, remote video 
terminals, and tactical operations centers. The system employs an 
extensive set of waveforms designed to ensure low latency, 
interoperable FMV distribution across joint and multinational networks. 
This system uses high assurance encryption.
    The highest level of classification of defense articles, 
components, and services included in this potential sale is SECRET.
    (vii) Date Report Delivered to Congress: October 16, 2026
